analysis.title: UBS TECH DAILY CURT COMMENT: Nvidia, ams, CBRS, AMAT, Wise
key_insights: Initial investor debates on Nvidia after the Jensen Huang resignation: how long before negative effects show up in products (c18 months?), more buybacks and less financing of the AI ecosystem, downside left in the share price, and how bullish this is for AVGO and AMD.
The author says he may have overstayed his bearish stance on semis, as he did with software. He sees no catalyst for semis to run and thinks software is too high again.

The author says Jensen's departure is a very big deal. As a buy-sider, he would want sell-siders to cut 2028 numbers by 20% to bridge the gap between semi estimates and data center powered shell (utility) estimates.
He disagrees that supply-side issues are already discounted after the 'blue sweep'. He thinks the bottom comes close only when estimates are cut.
Management teams, Jensen included, are 100% bullish all the time, so there are no good surprises. A reset would need an attitude change and an acknowledgement of double and triple ordering.
Current sell-side numbers may turn out roughly right, but near-perfect execution is needed to get there. The author asks tech analysts to risk-weight revenues as pharma analysts do.
CBRS (Cerebras) rose in the high teens after the market close on solid guidance. Bigger hardware sales more than offset delays in data center powered shell, which CBRS says affect the whole industry.

CBRS confirmed a new deal with MSFT (UBS thinks cloud-based, details scant). Together with the new OCI deal (UBS thinks hardware-based) and the early AMZN ramp, the customer base is diversifying. OpenAI remains by far the most important customer.

CBRS messaging on OpenAI was mixed. CBRS is not yet running GPT-6 Astra for public-facing instances, and the OpenAI part of RPO had net cuts. UBS attributes the cuts to powered shell delays that let OpenAI claim 'credits' against the contract.
UBS worries about the durability of the OpenAI relationship given personnel changes at OpenAI. CBRS stresses the contract is real take-or-pay with significant legal exposure for any backpedaling.
UBS (Tim) cut CBRS estimates and its price target to $155 on a more conservative OpenAI ramp. The rating stays Buy because UBS thinks the market has over-indexed to the OpenAI concern.

NVDA financing: Nvidia is a key source of funds for neo-clouds, LLM developers, ecosystem partners and suppliers. A new leader may pause these deals near term. UBS estimates NVDA generates ~$50-60B/Q of FCF, and ~$50B or more could leave the system at a time of rising rates and less liquid parts of the credit market.
NVDA supply chain: Nvidia is ahead of peers on long-term supply agreements in memory, substrates and other areas. UBS saw Jensen as singular in procurement.

NVDA China and Asia exposure: tighter US restrictions could hit shipments to China and to regions such as Singapore and Malaysia. Singapore was nearly 20% of revenue when Nvidia changed its geographic disclosure in mid-2025. UBS estimates roughly 10% of revenue could be at risk.

market_movers.rationale: Estimates and PT cut on a more conservative view of the OpenAI ramp. Rating stays Buy because UBS thinks the market has over-indexed to the OpenAI concern and guidance was solid.
Jensen Huang's resignation could pause ecosystem financing (~$50B or more), remove procurement leadership, and coincide with possible tighter export restrictions (~10% of revenue at risk).

sector_views.rationale: The author sees no catalyst for semis to run. He wants 2028 numbers cut by about 20%, and says the bottom comes only once estimates are cut.
The author thinks software is too high again.

earnings_insights: CBRS reported solid results and guidance well above expectations, as stated in the report (no figures given). Bigger hardware sales more than offset data center powered shell delays.
CBRS RPO: the OpenAI component had net cuts, which UBS attributes to powered shell delays that let OpenAI claim credits against the contract. This is not a reported EPS or revenue figure.
Upcoming MSFT results debrief call on the 19th and MCHP and QCOM IR calls on the 18th are listed. No estimates are given.
risk_factors: Pause in Nvidia's ecosystem financing (~$50B or more removed) while interest rates are rising and parts of the credit market are less liquid.
Loss of Jensen's lead on long-term supply agreements for memory, substrates and other inputs.
Tighter US export restrictions could put ~10% of NVDA revenue at risk (Singapore, Malaysia, China).
Data center powered shell delays across the industry.
CBRS concentration in OpenAI and personnel changes at OpenAI.
Double and triple ordering and 100%-bullish management teams leave sell-side numbers needing near-perfect execution.
vol_and_positioning: The author says he may have stayed bearish on semis too long, as he did with software, but sees no catalyst for semis to run.
Initial Nvidia debates include how much downside is left in the share price.
geopolitical: UBS sees a risk of tighter US export restrictions affecting NVDA and AMD shipments to China and to other regions such as Singapore and Malaysia.

tension_points.bull_case: The author concedes he may have overstayed his bearish view. Sell-side numbers may turn out roughly right, and investors debate how much downside is left in the share price and how bullish this is for AVGO and AMD.
tension_points.bear_case: Ecosystem financing could pause (~$50B or more), supply chain leadership is lost, and tighter export rules could put ~10% of revenue at risk. Estimates for 2028 need about a 20% cut.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The author says the bottom comes close only when sell-side numbers get cut. A 2028 estimate cut of about 20% would be the signal.

tension_points.bull_case: Guidance was well above expectations, bigger hardware sales offset powered shell delays, and the customer base is diversifying with MSFT, OCI and AMZN. The OpenAI contract is take-or-pay.
tension_points.bear_case: OpenAI is by far the most important customer. The OpenAI part of RPO was net cut, OpenAI may claim credits, and personnel changes at OpenAI raise durability concerns.
